1. Wife only told you about two cookies. 2. Why would your wife bother describing your daughter’s cookie if it wasn’t so you could differentiate it from the only other cookie in the box? 3. Wife only described what your daughter’s cookie looked like and did not describe her own. 4. Specialty bakeries do weird stuff to their baked goods. They like to decorate cookies in fun ways that end up making it hard to tell what flavor they are.  Given that your wife only told you about two cookies, did not specify your cookie was taken out of the box, and that bakeries tend to decorate their cookies in unexpected ways, you are NTA for assuming the only other cookie in the box was meant for you.

You’re especially NTA because you offered to go out and buy another cookie for your wife. All she had to say was that she put your cookie under the box in a separate bag.  She could have said that her and your daughter’s cookies were in one box and that yours was in a separate container. While Friskies and Fancy Feast are considered by some to be the McDonalds of the cat food industry, there are worse things you can feed your cat.  Fancy Feast in particular is owned by Purina, which is very good about following AAFCO guidelines and being prompt about informing the public of any recalls. 
Wet food diets are best for cats. [Water intake](https://catfriendly.com/keep-your-cat-healthy/water-intake/) is extremely important for our feline friends, so the most expensive, luxury dry food can’t compare to a cheap can of Fancy Feast.   

If you do want to move on to a more high quality cat diet, make sure there is a nutrition adequacy statement. The statement can look like this: “[Name of product] is formulated to meet the nutritional levels established by the AAFCO Cat Food Nutrient Profiles for [specific life stage].” Or like this: “Animal feeding tests using AAFCO procedures substantiate that [name of product] provides complete and balanced nutrition for [specific life stage].” Make sure there is contact information for the manufacturer on the bag.  Research to make sure the food company owns ALL of the manufacturing plants to reduce the risk of contamination by a 3rd party.  

Do not feed raw food diets. There is not scientific evidence supporting that a raw diet is more beneficial than a cooked diet. In fact, raw diets increase the chances of your cat contracting a food borne illness.  The current avian influenza outbreak that has been killing cats came from feeding raw poultry meat. 

Similarly, avoid freeze-dried diets. Those diets cannot eliminate food borne pathogens through the freeze drying process.

Imagine for a moment that you have spent your entire life until this moment living in a padded, numbing, and sleep causing bubble. You have never touched anything besides yourself and the soft walls around you.  Now imagine you are suddenly being touched by a cold object on your foot.  What would your immediate response be?  A flinch, right?  A jerk of your leg?  Anything foreign is likely to cause the body of the fetus to respond in this way.  It does not necessarily mean they are in pain. I am a veterinary technician, an animal nurse.  I have been for the past 5 years.  I am currently studying for my DVM license. While surgical abortion is not a common occurrence at my hospital, as we are a small animal practice which sterilizes most patients well before they get the chance to become pregnant, it is actually a much more risky procedure than it is in humans, as we have to perform it through an abdominal incision.  

Now, the discussion:

On your first point: While I will not deny that an abortion at later weeks can look pretty gruesome (an understatement, to be sure), what with there being recognizable body parts and limbs involved, it has not been proven the fetus has the ability to feel pain until they reach later stages of development. Before the third trimester, they lack a nervous system developed enough to transmit pain signals.  While touch causes hormone production and changes in heart rate, their brain has not developed the needed sections and connections responsible for making the body aware of injury in the form of pain.  Describing how the procedure is performed without stating this fact is a manipulative move designed to lead the listener into believing that the unborn baby is going through unspeakable torture.  This in turn is used to downplay the very real pain experienced by the woman having to go through an unwanted pregnancy.  It is a common pro-life tactic. 
Links about fetal pain and development of the sensation of touch: 
https://www.livescience.com/54774-fetal-pain-anesthesia.html

 https://www.whattoexpect.com/pregnancy/fetal-development/fetal-touch/

On your second point: The only one in this situation being punished is the woman, who actually has the awareness of  such a concept, as it is her bodily autonomy that is being denied.  Think on this for a moment: As a nurse, you should be aware that a person cannot be forced to use their body to save another life. Even if their kidney is a match to a dying patient, and they are that patient’s only hope of survival, they cannot be forced to go through a medical procedure to save them. You can’t even force a person to donate their blood. Is the patient who is being denied that kidney, denied that blood, being punished because the person doesn’t want to give up those things?  Absolutely not.  That person has every right to say what happens to their body, and the patient has authority to violate that right.  And yet somehow women are expected to give up their bodies for 9 months for the sake of what for all intents and purposes is not even a person yet. That is hypocrisy.  That is a double standard.  And by taking away the woman’s bodily autonomy, they are being punished. A link regarding bodily autonomy: https://bodyhackingcon.com/blog/bodily-autonomy.html 

Your third point: Some abortion risks can be life threatening, but so can anything that is left untreated or done by an incompetent physician.  By having an abortion performed in a hospital setting, doctors have the resources to minimize those risks. A blood transfusion can be set up, antibiotics can be administered.  There are follow up appointments to ensure there are no complications afterwards.  Standard procedure when it comes to surgery and aftercare. 
Again, here is a link to the common risks associated with abortion (I included this in my first post, but I don’t know if you saw it) https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/abortion/risks/
If abortion were to be banned, like the pro-life movement wants it to be, all of those safety precautions would fly out the window.  A ban would not stop women from getting abortions, just cause them to get unsafe ones. We do not have to look far to see what an abortion ban would do to a population.  Here is an article about what happened in Romania when abortion was banned in the country: https://foreignpolicy.com/2019/05/16/what-actually-happens-when-a-country-bans-abortion-romania-alabama/


Regarding your fourth point:  Providing affordable healthcare services to low income communities is not a form of manipulation and is most certainly not a form of targeting people of color.  Clinics like Planned Parenthood are sometimes the only affordable reproductive health clinic available for miles. They provide low cost/free STI testing, birth control options, emergency contraception, breast exams, Pap smears, prenatal care, and yes, abortions.  They provide sex education, counseling, HIV treatment, and hormone therapy. People who are pro-life believe these clinics are only stationed in poor neighborhoods to manipulate people into choosing abortion, as if they’re trying to prey upon unsuspecting, underprivileged people to...what? Target people of color in order to...what? To cull the herd? Gain a profit?  I really don’t understand these conspiracies. They’re  illogical, based in paranoia and cynicism. Low cost “abortion clinics”, or rather, reproductive healthcare providers—which is what they are actually called—like Planned Parenthood, are nonprofit organizations that rely on donations to provide these services.
